expo.name: The Poker Club
expo.//slug: MUST MATCH THE PROJECT ON expo.dev, which is poker-cash-games-manager — not the app's name, and not this repo's. `eas update` compares this field against the slug of the project named by extra.eas.projectId and refuses to publish when they disagree, which is how the first successful-looking publish failed: token fine, project found, slug wrong. The display name above is what a person sees and is free to differ.
expo.//: Two themes, dark and light — the OS decides which. Never pin this to one.
expo.//scheme: Watchers open a share link that deep-links straight into the session.
expo.//updates: NOT IN THIS FILE, ON PURPOSE — and no longer missing either: app.config.js adds updates.url and runtimeVersion when EAS_PROJECT says which kind of build is being made. BOTH cases carry a runtimeVersion and they differ: Expo Go is one fixed native build calling itself exposdk:54.0.0 and opens only updates stamped to match, while a standalone build stamps the app version. Leave it out and eas update writes the standalone one in for you, publishes happily, and the phone silently will not open it. Read the comment in app.config.js before changing this.
expo.//eas: THE EAS PROJECT ID IS NOT IN THIS FILE, ON PURPOSE. An id here makes Expo Go prompt for an Expo login on every start, which breaks the scan-a-QR-code loop for no benefit while developing. app.config.js adds it — with updates.url, and with runtimeVersion when a standalone build asks for it — only when EAS_PROJECT is set, so publishing and developing each get the config they need. The project is 938b4629-9a41-4ddf-bcd8-86bb4e4696b3, and app.config.js is the one place it is written down.
